title: Microsegment Prospect Thread: SaaS Support & Knowledge Workflows (Draft)
content:
Context and intent:
- Purpose: compact prospect-facing slide set + short battlecard for AE/SE to run discovery and a 20–30 minute technical scoping call for SaaS vendors building support/knowledge workflows (help centers, in-app chat, enterprise support desks).
- Goal: rapid qualification -> 1) fit for Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted, 2) recommended integration pattern (API vs Private), 3) 3-step pilot plan and numbers to justify a POC.

Audience persona (one-liners):
- Product Lead (Support): cares about latency for agent chat, retrieval relevance, data residency.
- Platform/Infra Lead: asks about VPC, SSO, model updates, and throughput guarantees.
- CS/Rev Ops: wants clear ROI story vs current vector DB + LLM host costs.

Slide-by-slide (speaker notes inline):
1) Opening slide — "Support automation that keeps agents faster and customers happier"
   Speaker note: open with 30s of pain: ticket deflection dropped, response SLAs slipping, search relevance low.

2) Quick qualification checklist (one-slide diagnostic)
   - Avg concurrent agents? (estimate: 25–500)
   - % of requests requiring retrieval/KB lookup? (>70% -> retrieval-heavy)
   - PII/Sensitive content? yes/no -> flags Private deployment
   - Latency SLO target for agent UI: <150ms per token or <250ms end-to-end?

3) Where problems show up (battlecard bullets)
   - Slow token throughput from long context (multi-turn tickets)
   - Inconsistent answers as KB evolves (no pinned model versions)
   - Cost spike from naive batching or long prefixes

4) Redwood fit map (quick mapping grid)
   - Hosted API: fast time-to-value, good for small-mid SaaS with non-sensitive data
   - Dedicated: predictable throughput and isolation for scale (>100 concurrent agents)
   - Private: for regulated customers, strict residency/KMS + air-gapped option

5) Technical win patterns (three recommended integration archetypes)
   - Agent UI augmentation (streaming responses + prefix caching) — best single-node ROI
   - Retrieval-augmented generation with staged KV cache (short-term + long-term) — reduces tokens by 30–60% in bench tests
   - Hybrid routing: session affinity to Dedicated instances with fallback to Hosted during bursts

6) Performance vs spend quick sheet (talking numbers)
   - Example baseline: 1M messages/month, avg 200 tokens/request -> raw hosted compute cost X
   - With caching + batching: expect 30% lower token spend and 20% latency reduction (bench: internal support workload, Q2 2025)
   - When to recommend Dedicated: sustained throughput >500k tokens/hour or predictable SLA needs

7) Objections and replies (short scripts)
   - "We can just host an open model ourselves": reply -> ops cost, kernel tuning, and continuous batching are non-trivial; Redwood maintains tuned kernels + rollout tools and handles fallbacks.
   - "Latency concerns for agent UI": reply -> show prefix caching + streaming demo + Dedicated SLOs; propose 2-week latency benchmark.
   - "Cost is unknown": reply -> propose a pilot with instrumentation (Console trace + token-level cost) and fixed pilot cap.

8) Pilot / POC plan (30 days)
   - Week 0–1: integration + test dataset (5–10k support transcripts), enable prefix cache, route a sample cohort of agents
   - Week 2: tune batch sizes, enable retrieval TTL, run bench against sample traffic window
   - Week 3–4: QA, AB test vs baseline metrics (FRT, deflection, agent satisfaction) -> deliver final ROI sheet

9) Playbook snippets for AE/SE (scripts + follow-ups)
   - Prospect opener email (1-liner): "We help support teams reduce time-to-resolution by making agent context cheaper and faster — quick 15m to see a tailored latency/cost sketch?"
   - Discovery question set (top 8): concurrent users, % retrieval, avg doc length, existing vector stack, SSO/KMS needs, expected growth, busiest timezone, acceptable pilot cap
   - Demo checklist: live streaming sample, toggle cache on/off, show cost dashboard per-route, show model rollouts and fallback triggers

10) Simple handshake: What we need to run a pilot
   - Small anonymized transcript dump (5–10k lines), API key for test environment, contact for infra + product, pilot cap ($X or tokens)

11) Risks, mitigations, and unresolved items (internal)
   - Risk: large historical KB migrations create initial cold-cache blowup -> Mitigation: staged seeding + TTL-based warming
   - Unresolved: what threshold of PII forces Private? -> action: validate with security team on specific data types (ticket includes attachments vs inline PII)

Appendix (one-slide each)
- Live demo steps (detailed): how to reproduce streaming + fallback scenario
- Benchmark methodology: synthetic vs real-session capture notes
- Quick tech map: supported model families, quantization/kv cache notes, preferred GPU families for Dedicated

Action items / TODOs
- [ ] Add final numbers from Q3 support workload bench (Maya)
- [ ] Build sample email templates for AE sequences (Rajat)
- [ ] Ask Security to confirm PII gating thresholds for Private (Drew)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this under 10 slides; AE should be able to run the 20–30m call without SE for initial discovery.
- Avoid heavy marketing language; use measurable outcomes (FRT, % deflection, token cost delta).
- Consider a one-pager for CS owner that maps to renewal conversations (ops cost savings).

Related links and quick refs:
- internal bench doc: confluence.redwood/support-bench-Q3-2025 (draft)
- demo repo: github.com/redwood-inference/demos/support-streaming

Questions for review:
- Is the pilot cap framing ($ or tokens) better as a fixed $ cap for prospects? (seems easier for finance approval)
- Should we include a price-band example for Dedicated reserved capacity for midmarket (25–100k tokens/min sustained)?

End.
